messages:
sam: noticing steady memory climb on staging when clients use long streaming toolloops (30-40k tokens). Started after the prefetch/predictor change last week.

maya: saw similar in prod can confirm on a few Dedicated nodes. Not an OOM but resident set keeps growing over hours.

arjun: quick repro? I can run a long streamer locally if you share the script.

sam: here's a small reproducer we used (python):

```python
# stream_toolloop_repro.py - repeatedly call streaming chat with tool-calls
for i in range(1000):
    resp = client.chat.stream(messages=long_prompt, tools=[...])
    for chunk in resp:
        process(chunk)
```

sam: attached pmap + smaps snapshot from a node after ~6 hours: RSS grows ~850MB over baseline, anonymous mappings cluster around kv_pool slabs.

maya: pasted relevant lines:

```
7f8b9c0000-7f8b9d0000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0          [anon:kv_slab:slot-idx=12]
7f8b9d0000-7f8b9f0000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0          [anon:kv_slab:slot-idx=13]
... repeated many nearby addresses ...
```

lee: that's suspicious — slots should be recycled after tool completion. Are holds/pin counts being cleared?

arjun: I profiled refcounts around the hot path. Flamegraph shows stack:

```
serving::ToolLoop::step
serving::KVCache::pin_for_stream
serving::KVSlot::retain
// no symmetric release in this codepath for edge case where tool raises ToolAbort
```

sam: good find. Also noticed the prefetcher recently introduced an async warmup that pins slots earlier. If a tool aborts before warming finishes, we might leave a pinned ref.

maya: perf-bot ran the nightly heap diff and flagged +70MB over baseline in kv_slot objects. diff attached.

perf-bot: CI heap-diff report: https://ci.redwood/heapdiff/3133 -> suspects: KVSlot::pinned_count (delta +120)

lee: can we repro a minimal C++ trace that shows missing unpin? I can add asserts into the pin/unpin code to catch mismatches.

arjun: I pushed a small instrument branch: `kv-pin-assert`. With that enabled, running the repro triggered an assertion after ~150 iterations: "kvslot: pin_count mismatch on destroy".

sam: results align. So two contributing factors: prefetch warmup pins early, and tool abort path skips unpin. Combined they form small persistent "heaplets" that accumulate across long sessions.

maya: proposed mitigations:
- ensure tool abort + early-exit paths run symmetric unpin cleanup (quick PR)
- add a timed background compaction that will forcibly evict slots with stale last-touch > X when under mem pressure (safer short-term)
- reduce prefetch window when streaming long contexts to avoid aggressive pinning

lee: also worth checking kernel selection changes — the new memcpy-kernel path increases allocation churn for small KV pages; maybe fragmentation + pinned tiny slabs prevents coalescing. I can run kernel A/B.

arjun: I ran a quick experiment swapping kernel to legacy copy path. RSS growth rate drops ~30% during the repro. That suggests fragmentation exacerbates the leak.

sam: action items:
- arjun: PR to add unpin in all tool-abort/exception branches (small, high priority)
- lee: roll kernel A/B on a subset and collect pmap + fragmentation histogram (48h)
- maya: implement a lightweight compaction job that runs on Dedicated nodes when RSS > threshold (configurable)
- perf-bot: add heap-diff check on nightly for KVSlot pins and kv_slab anon maps

arjun: created PR #4122 with cleanup, added unit tests to simulate tool aborts. Requesting reviews from lee/maya.

maya: I'll prototype compaction. Idea: maintain per-slab freelist plus epoch-based reclaim that can migrate live slots to lower-fragment slabs during quiet cycles.

lee: for the kernel change, I'll instrument the allocator to expose fragmentation ratio and preferred kernel counts. If we can detect heavy fragmentation we can bias the kernel choice away from the small-mem-copy path.

sam: great. One more diagnostic I want added: export kv_slot.pin_count and kv_slot.last_touch as metrics with histograms (1s resolution) so we can observe long-tail pin durations in prod.

arjun: added metrics to the instrument branch, will wire to console dashboard.

maya: TL;DR: leak appears to be a correctness hole (missing unpin) amplified by prefetch/pinning + small-copy kernel that increases fragmentation. Short-term fix = unpin PR + reduce prefetch window. Medium = compaction + kernel bias.

sam: thanks all. I'll schedule a canary deploy of the unpin fix to staging tonight and monitor. Please post results here. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: deploy canary to staging: job/serving-canary-3133 started.

lee: quick note: if compaction will migrate live pages it might impact latency during bursts — we should schedule it during low-qps windows.

arjun: agreed. We'll gate compaction behind a mem-pressure + low-qps signal.

maya: staging canary looks clean for 6h, RSS plateaued instead of climbing. Pushing to small prod canary next.

sam: bump when prod canary is green or if any regressions show.
